page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-32 is an arm64-based server instance powered by the Neoverse-V2 processor architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration, providing 32 vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications consist of 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and an 80 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4a-standard-32 demonstrates strong memory subsystem performance. PassMark memory testing places the instance in the top tier, supported by uncached read bandwidth of 343.0 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 161.74 GB/sec. Database operations are highly efficient, with PassMark database testing scoring in the top tier and Redis SET operations reaching 68.8 million operations per second. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, falls within the average range, while single-threaded gzip compression and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression show strong throughput. For machine learning workloads, the server achieves average prompt processing speeds and strong text generation speeds of 31.42 tokens per second on medium 7B LLM models.

The arm64 architecture of the c4a-standard-32 offers a resource-dense profile that delivers high memory bandwidth and database processing efficiency relative to its hardware class. The lack of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it a specialized option for network-attached storage configurations. This instance is suited for memory-bound applications, database operations, static web serving, and medium-scale language model inference tasks where dedicated physical cores and high memory throughput are required.
